text.p: Colombian striker Faustino Asprilla has failed to return from international duty to his English club side Newcastle.

Asprilla, who has found himself on the substitutes' bench at the premier league club of late, has been in South America, where he scored for Colombia in their 1-0 World Cup win in Ecuador on Wednesday.
He missed an appointment with a Newcastle official in London on Friday and has not contacted the club since.
"We don't know where he is," manager Kevin Keegan said as he prepared for Saturday's league match at Derby.
"We have received a fax from Colombia saying that the plane was stranded. We know that it has since taken off but we don't know where Tino is."

Asprilla, who joined Newcastle from Italy's Parma for a then-club-record 7.5 million pounds ($11.8 million) last season, was axed from the Colombian squad in March after missing a training session in Medellin.
He was eventually re-instated after arriving a day late and telling the national team coach he had had "a family problem" to attend to.
Asprilla was rumoured last week to be seeking a return to Italy because of his failure to secure a first-team place at St James' Park.
But he denied the reports, saying: "I'm happy in England and I'm staying at Newcastle. (Talks of a move) are just rumours."
